newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says would consider sale of alloys unit.
newsitem.headline: Inco says would consider sale of alloys unit.

text.p: Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd said on Wednesday that it would consider selling its alloys subsidiary for the right price.
Inco President Scott Hand said the alloys unit was delivering good profits and cash flow, but that Inco wanted to focus on its core nickel operations.

"Our strategy is nickel and if someone comes and offers us the right price, and I stress the right price, we're going to have to consider it very seriously," Hand told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
In its first quarter report on Tuesday, Inco said operating results from its alloys unit improved significantly due to higher shipments and lower raw materials costs.
The alloys business reported operating earnings of US$16 million in first quarter of 1997, compared to US$6 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, and US$15 million in the first quarter of 1996.
The alloys unit posted first quarter sales of US$173 million, compared to US$164 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, and US$171 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Inco's first quarter 1997 results included an after-tax gain of US$36 million from the sale of Doncasters Plc, through an initial public offering last February.
Inco received gross proceeds of US$132 million from the Doncasters transaction.
